int_name: N 5TH ST & W HUNTING PARK AVE

result.summary: The intersection features a wide roadway with a marked zebra crosswalk but lacks pedestrian refuge islands or visible pedestrian signals. The surrounding environment is primarily industrial and commercial, with wide lanes that may encourage higher vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross a wide roadway without a median refuge, increasing exposure time to traffic.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible at this signalized intersection, leaving pedestrians to rely on vehicle signals.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles on the left side of the image may block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians entering the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility of pedestrians by moving them into the driver's line of sight.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Add a raised island in the center of the roadway to allow pedestrians to cross in two stages and provide a safe waiting area.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Signal Installation
interventions.description: Install countdown pedestrian signals to provide clear right-of-way information and improve safety at the signalized crossing.

result.summary: The image shows a signalized intersection with marked zebra crosswalks, pedestrian signals, and sidewalks on both sides. While basic infrastructure is present, the wide roadway and parked vehicles near the crossing create potential visibility and exposure risks for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars on the right side of the street near the crosswalk may block the line of sight between drivers and pedestrians entering the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street, adjacent to the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide roadway increases the time pedestrians are exposed to traffic without a median refuge.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the image across the roadway.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the intersection to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features basic infrastructure like sidewalks and a marked crosswalk, but lacks robust safety measures. The wide roadway and faded markings suggest a priority for vehicle throughput over pedestrian safety.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk
hazards.description: The zebra markings are significantly worn, making the crossing less visible to approaching motorists.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb line block the view of pedestrians waiting to cross.

hazards.name: Lack of Traffic Control
hazards.description: No stop signs or signals are visible to manage vehicle flow at the pedestrian crossing.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Repaint the crossing with high-visibility continental markings to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and improve sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking within 20 feet of the intersection to ensure clear sightlines.

result.summary: The intersection features marked zebra crosswalks and overhead traffic signals within a mixed-use urban environment. However, the lack of visible pedestrian-specific signals and the presence of parked vehicles near the crossing points create potential visibility and safety gaps for people walking.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection corners obstruct the sightlines between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs on both sides of the main roadway approaching the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible, forcing pedestrians to rely on vehicular signals which may not provide adequate clearance time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to clear sightlines.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear information on crossing time.
